meta.title: Ondra Cross-Device Prerequisites
meta.description: The prerequisite entry point for the three-device setup, shipped as a skeleton. The ledger gives nine characters of guidance: placeholder, pin down the technical prerequisites. This package does not build a mobile client, because the handbook says the phone is coming soon, and a window built ahead of that only produces installed but empty. Instead it pins the facts scattered across three places in the handbook into seven checkable prerequisites: one shared memory, the pet entry present, a local HTTP exit, a wired WebSocket relay, allowed origins configured, matching tokens on both sides, and a released mobile client. Verdicts use four values rather than a boolean: what structurally cannot be verified says so, and what is not released says so. Squashing unverifiable into false sends people to fix something that is not broken, and squashing it into true sends them to trust a setup that shows three separate memories. Binding one account to two platforms, or replacing a platform peer without unbinding, is refused rather than silently overwritten, because an overwrite means it was her yesterday and someone else today while the log looks perfectly normal. The relay address rule deliberately differs from the desktop pet bridge: the phone is not on this machine, so what matters is encrypted wss across devices, and copying the loopback allow-list would leave the phone permanently unable to connect while appearing configured. No tool is registered and no frame format is defined, since cross-device relay is infrastructure rather than a model action.
